document_check.note: The document is Yakoub Y, Gonzalez-Ortiz F, Ashton NJ et al., 'Plasma p-tau217 identifies cognitively normal older adults who will develop cognitive impairment in a 10-year window', Alzheimer's & Dementia 2025;21:e14537. The cited plasma A+T+ HR of 7.81 (3.92 to 15.59) for progression from cognitively unimpaired to MCI, against the A−T− reference, matches the document.

cited_result: Cox proportional hazards: plasma A+T+ (Aβ42/40 and p-tau217) vs A−T− reference, HR 7.81 (95% CI 3.92 to 15.59), for progression from cognitively unimpaired to MCI (n = 215; 16/21 A+T+ and 25/127 A−T− progressed).
tool_reason: The cited result is a hazard ratio linking one prognostic factor, plasma amyloid/tau status, with later progression to MCI. It is not the performance of a multivariable prediction model, so QUIPS applies.

domains.rationale: The source population, inclusion criteria, period and baseline sample are well described. The sample is a volunteer cohort enriched for first-degree family history of AD (98% White, 72% female). Inclusion required available plasma biomarkers and at least 1 year of follow-up, with a plasma time point chosen by PET availability. The number of eligible PREVENT-AD participants and the participation proportion are given only in a supplementary figure that is not in the document.

signalling.question: Is the source population adequately described?
signalling.quote: We included 215 participants from the Presymptomatic Evaluation of Experimental or Novel Treatments for Alzheimer Disease (PREVENT-AD) cohort, a longitudinal observational study of individuals with a first-degree family history of AD (Figure S1 in supporting information).

signalling.question: Are inclusion and exclusion criteria adequately described?
signalling.quote: Participants included in this study were CU based on an extensive neuropsychological evaluation at the time of the biomarker assessment and had a minimum of 1 year of cognitive follow-up thereafter.

signalling.question: Is the period and place of recruitment described?
signalling.quote: Longitudinal data collected between 2011 and 2023 ... all research procedures were approved by the institutional review board at McGill University

signalling.question: Was there adequate participation of eligible persons?
signalling.quote: Searched the main text for the number of eligible PREVENT-AD participants, exclusions and a participation proportion; the flow is referred to 'Figure S1 in supporting information', which is not in the document.

signalling.question: Is the sampling of the baseline time point independent of the prognostic factor and outcome?
signalling.quote: Plasma and CSF time points closest to the PET scans were selected for this study ... For individuals who did not have PET scans, the plasma sample closest to 2017 was taken.

signalling.question: Does the baseline sample represent the population of interest?
signalling.quote: One main limitation is the low racial, ethnic (98% White), and sex imbalance (72% female) of our population, as the findings may not be generalizable to all populations.

domains.rationale: Follow-up ranged from 1.01 to 10.47 years after plasma classification, and losses are handled only as censoring in the survival analysis. The main text reports no proportion lost, no reasons for loss and no comparison of those lost with those followed. Requiring at least 1 year of follow-up removed early losses from the sample.

signalling.question: Was the proportion followed up adequate?
signalling.quote: The mean cognitive follow-up was 5.65 years (SD = 1.45, range 1.01–10.47) after plasma classification (no proportion lost to follow-up reported).

signalling.question: Were attempts to collect information on those who dropped out, and reasons for loss to follow-up, described?
signalling.quote: Searched for 'lost to follow-up', 'withdrew', 'dropout', 'attrition'; the only statement is 'The vertical ticks on the curves refer to censored participants, that is, the lack of follow-up of the individuals.'

signalling.question: Were there no important differences between participants who completed follow-up and those who did not?
signalling.quote: Searched for a comparison of completers and non-completers by AT status or baseline characteristics; none reported.

signalling.question: Did the eligibility rule exclude early losses?
signalling.quote: had a minimum of 1 year of cognitive follow-up thereafter

domains.rationale: Plasma p-tau217 and Aβ42/40 were measured in one specialised laboratory with defined assays. Positivity thresholds were pre-established or derived from Aβ PET-negative CU participants, not from progression status. Complete prognostic factor data were guaranteed by the inclusion rule. Laboratory blinding to outcome is not stated, but the outcome accrued after sampling and the assays are quantitative.

signalling.question: Is the prognostic factor clearly defined, with cut-points not derived from the outcome?
signalling.quote: For the binary analyses, plasma and CSF p-tau217 levels were set at 2 standard deviation (SD) above the mean of Aβ PET–negative individuals who were CU from the PREVENT-AD cohort (plasma p-tau217: 3.98 pg/mL; CSF p-tau217: 400.19 pg/mL). ... We used the pre-established thresholds of 0.09 for plasma Aβ42/40 and 0.072 for CSF Aβ42/40.

signalling.question: Is the method of measurement valid and reliable?
signalling.quote: Plasma and CSF p-tau217 were measured using an in-house Simoa platform developed at the Clinical Neurochemistry Laboratory, University of Gothenburg. ... plasma and CSF biomarkers are known to be more prone to measurement errors, matrix effects, and batch-to-batch variability compared to PET.

signalling.question: Was the same method and setting used for all participants?
signalling.quote: Plasma Aβ40 and Aβ42 concentrations were measured using ultrasensitive immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry (IP-MS) technique using a KingFisher Flex Purification System (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at the Clinical Neurochemistry Laboratory.

signalling.question: Does an adequate proportion of the sample have complete prognostic factor data?
signalling.quote: We included 215 participants from the PREVENT−AD cohort with plasma Aβ42/40 and p-tau217

signalling.question: Was the prognostic factor measured without knowledge of the outcome?
signalling.quote: Searched section 2.1 for blinding of laboratory staff to clinical status; blinding is stated only for the outcome classification.

domains.rationale: MCI was defined explicitly (RBANS or RAVLT deviation from demographically stratified norms, plus complaint or witnessed decline). It was adjudicated by a multidisciplinary consensus blind to plasma, CSF, PET, MRI and APOE, using the same battery throughout follow-up.

signalling.question: Is the outcome clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Individuals with a cognitive performance deviating by more than 1.0 SD from demographically stratified norms on at least one of the five composite subscale scores ... of the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS), or on two subset scores on the Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test (RAVLT) were revised in consensus. ... to be classified as MCI, participants needed to have a subjective memory complaint

signalling.question: Is the outcome measured validly and reliably, blind to the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: MCI classification was determined in a reserch setting based on a multidisciplinary consensus meeting comprising dementia specialist neuropsychologists (SV and MM) and physicians (SD and MG). ... All MCI classification was performed blind to plasma, CSF, PET, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype information.

signalling.question: Was the same method and setting of outcome measurement used for all participants?
signalling.quote: The RBANS is administered to PREVENT-AD participants throughout the entire study follow-up.

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education and APOE were measured. The methods sentence is ambiguous about whether age, sex and education were covariates in the Cox models, and the figure legend attaches them to the linear mixed models only. The cited HR is reported without a statement of adjustment. APOE is not listed as a covariate for any model.

signalling.question: Were important potential confounders measured?
signalling.quote: The mean age of the full sample at baseline was 63 years, 72% were female, and 39% were APOE ε4 carriers.

signalling.question: Were important confounders accounted for in the analysis of the cited hazard ratio?
signalling.quote: Cox proportional hazard models were used to assess the risk of MCI progression by AT group and linear mixed models were used to assess longitudinal cognitive changes across the biomarker groups with the addition of age at the biomarker classification, sex, and years of education as covariates. ... The linear mixed effects models analyses included annual cognitive data before and after plasma, CSF, and PET measures. Models included age at biomarker measurement, sex, and years of education as covariates.

signalling.question: Was APOE genotype accounted for?
signalling.quote: Searched every covariate statement for APOE; it appears only in the descriptive sample table and in blinding statements, not in any model specification.

domains.rationale: Group counts and events are presented, and non-significant contrasts are reported, so there is no sign of selective reporting. However, the HR rests on 16 events among 21 A+T+ participants, against a reference group in which 20% progressed. The authors themselves ask for caution. The proportional-hazards assumption is not reported as checked, and the Cox model specification is incompletely described.

signalling.question: Is there sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis?
signalling.quote: Seventy-six percent (16/21) of the A+T+plasma group developed MCI compared to 23% (14/60) in the A+T−plasma group, 71% (5/7) in the A−T+plasma group, and 21% (25/127) in the A−T−plasma group

signalling.question: Is the statistical model adequate for the design, with assumptions checked?
signalling.answer: Probably yes for the model choice; No information on assumptions
signalling.quote: Cox proportional hazard models showed a higher risk of progression from CU to MCI among the A+T+plasma and A−T+plasma (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.81, P < 0.001, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.92 to 15.59; (searched for 'proportional hazards assumption', 'Schoenfeld'; none found)

signalling.question: Are the data sufficient for a stable estimate?
signalling.quote: The low sample size in the A+T+ and the A−T+ groups should also be noted. ... Given this limitation and the fact that 20% of our reference group developed MCI, the HRs between groups should be interpreted with caution.

signalling.question: Is there no selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: There were no differences between A+T−plasma and A−T−plasma group (HR = 1.14, P = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.58 to 2.24).

applicability.rationale: A family-history-enriched research cohort (98% White, 72% female, mean education about 15.3 years). The HR may not transfer to unselected older adults with normal cognition.

The exposure is combined plasma A+T+ status, using an in-house Simoa p-tau217 assay, an IP-MS Aβ42/40 assay and cohort-specific thresholds (3.98 pg/mL; 0.09). It is not p-tau217 alone and not a commercial assay threshold.
All-cause MCI by blinded research consensus matches the review's 'progression from normal cognition to MCI'.

overall: High risk of bias by the review's QUIPS rule (four domains moderate: participation, attrition, confounding, statistical analysis; prognostic factor and outcome measurement low; no single domain high).
overall_rationale: Measurement of the prognostic factor and outcome is strong: thresholds are pre-specified and MCI adjudication is blind. The high overall rating comes from the review's count rule (three or more moderate domains), not from any single serious flaw. The moderate domains are: participation and attrition not reported in the main text (the flow is in a supplement that is not in the document); ambiguity over whether the Cox HR was adjusted for age, sex and education, with no APOE adjustment; and a sparse index group of 16 events among 21 participants, with no reported check of proportional hazards. If the supplementary flow showed adequate participation and follow-up, the rating would fall to some concerns.
